narrative.rule: a decision says what holds, in the present tense or as an instruction — not who decided it, when, or what was done
narrative.rewrites: "<The thing> uses <the choice> for <the purpose>" or "Use <the choice> for <the purpose>, not <the other>"

hints.kind_retired: kind must be correction, runbook, gotcha or decision. An incident's reusable clause is a gotcha; a fact with a command trigger is a gotcha; a state-of-the-world statement is not memory at all
hints.too_long: content is one imperative sentence of at most 220 characters — put the reasoning, the exact commands and the paths in detail
hints.detail_too_long: detail is at most 1200 characters — this is a memory, not a write-up
hints.not_one_sentence: content is ONE sentence — everything after the first full stop belongs in detail
hints.status_not_memory: this is the state of the world today, not something that will still be true next month; write the rule you learned instead, or nothing
hints.not_imperative: content must start with an instruction (Use, Never, Always, Run, Check, Before, When …); a correction may instead read "X is/must/stays Y", and a decision may be any statement of what holds
hints.no_trigger: a runbook or gotcha nobody can be warned about is unreachable — pass the verbatim command or error keywords in triggers
hints.burst: batch settled findings at the end of the task; one atom per fact
hints.not_a_decision: alternatives and reason_status describe a decision: what was ruled out, and whether a reason was given. This kind has neither
hints.reason_missing: a decision says why. Put the reason in detail. If there is none on record, say which case it is: reason_status="not_stated" when nobody has answered why yet (not asked, or the question was skipped); reason_status="no_strong_reason" when the developer was asked and said there was no particular reason
hints.reason_contradiction: detail and reason_status disagree: stated needs a reason in detail, and not_stated means there is no reason to put in detail. no_strong_reason may carry the developer's own words about why there is none
hints.alternatives_too_many: alternatives holds at most 6 options of at most 220 characters each — one rejected option per entry, the reasoning in detail

examples.kind_retired: kind="gotcha", content="Never set EPHEMERAL in the runner compose file", triggers=["EPHEMERAL", "fylgja-runner"]
examples.too_long: content="Run alembic upgrade head before starting the worker" with the reasoning moved into detail
examples.detail_too_long: detail: the exact command plus one paragraph of why — not the transcript
examples.not_one_sentence: content="Use `just test-db` for the database tiers" — the second sentence belongs in detail
examples.status_not_memory: nothing — a PR status is not memory. If a rule came out of it, write that: content="Always rebase onto main before requesting review", kind="runbook"
examples.not_imperative: content="Never run terraform apply without -target on the GPU stack" (runbook/gotcha), or content="The live database is fylgja_rebuild" (decision/correction)
examples.no_trigger: triggers=["docker volume rm", "fylgja-runner"] — the words that appear in the command itself
examples.burst: one call at the end of the task carrying the one thing that will still be true tomorrow
examples.not_a_decision: kind="decision" with the reason in detail — or leave alternatives and reason_status out
examples.reason_missing: detail="Chosen because the worker already holds a Redis connection", or reason_status="not_stated", or reason_status="no_strong_reason"
examples.reason_contradiction: the reason in detail and no reason_status; or no detail and reason_status="not_stated"; or reason_status="no_strong_reason" with or without the developer's own words in detail
examples.alternatives_too_many: alternatives=["Postgres advisory locks", "a Redis lock"] — the options really weighed
